correctness.rationale: Complete quantified proof for \(n\ge 2k+1\) and \(k\ge1\): orbital quotient \(B(t,u)\), binomial-function triangularization with \(k+1\) distinct eigenvalues, vertex-transitive nonzero projectors, Vandermonde cyclicity of the root indicator, and colour-refinement invariance imply all \(k+1\) intersection strata are separated by round k. Binomial counts to the \(t=0\) class prove the iff two-round criterion at \(k\ge3\); a non-skipping shell walk proves the exact odd-graph depth \(k-1\). n=2k, k=1, k=2 handled explicitly. Independent full graph and quotient checker ran successfully; finite tests are not used as universal proof.

originality.rationale: The contribution is a single-root counting-refinement theorem across all connected Kneser graphs, including a sharp two-round boundary \(n\ge 3k-2\) and an exact (\(k-1\))-round delay at the odd-graph boundary. value.rationale: A single coloured root is the minimal vertex-individualization experiment; the Kneser family changes connectivity and local disjoint-neighbour counts as n crosses linear density thresholds. The result quantifies exact stable orbit information and a sharp two-round transition at n=3k-2, while showing unbounded \(k-1\) refinement delay on odd graphs. Both effects hold along infinite natural families, and the class sizes are explicit. This is not an arbitrary finite census.
